purpose: Generate source-grounded ECDLP research questions from compatible target features, mechanism primitives, and unresolved cost-changing questions; compile model- or human-authored answers through adversarial review before they may enter candidate intake.

trust_boundary.creative_output: A generated seed or proposer-authored mechanism is untrusted research input. It may be novel, mistaken, duplicated, or merely a renamed representation.
trust_boundary.deterministic_engine: The deterministic layer checks provenance, scope, exact required fields, known-premise fingerprints, review coverage, and authorization boundaries. It does not prove mathematical novelty or truth.
trust_boundary.quality_claim: Quality-cleared means that every declared hard gate and five-role review gate passed for the exact proposal digest. It does not mean the hypothesis is true, novel in all literature, or likely to break ECDLP.
trust_boundary.authorization_boundary: This layer never authorizes an experiment, promotes a route, targets secp256k1 directly, or makes an asymptotic claim.

typed_evidence_contract.decision_rule: Only a materialized typed cell marked seed-eligible may enter synthesis; violated or closed cells are retained as scoped desk decisions and produce no creative prompt.

fingerprint_contract.premise_limitation: The premise digest catches exact normalized duplicates only. Lexical near-duplicates are flagged as semantic re-encoding risks and require adversarial review; neither check proves mathematical equivalence.
fingerprint_contract.near_duplicate_policy: All same-route premise pairs above the fixed lexical threshold enter one visible collision audit and cannot quality-clear until the semantic re-encoding risk is removed.

quality_gate.overflow_rule: If more than three proposals clear every quality gate, retain none automatically and require an explicit comparative portfolio decision; do not silently truncate or rank by model confidence.

known_premises.basis: Replace every Semaev relation coordinate independently by u_i = x_i^3 and treat all erased GLV phases as equivalent for the same fixed target.
Process R, phi(R), and phi^2(R) as a finite target batch and infer a nonconstant asymptotic reduction from the order-three orbit alone.
Treat confirmation of a known division-polynomial or torsion identity as evidence that a discrete-log attack mechanism was positively tested.

target_features.label: the exact order-three GLV action on the j=0 curve
target_features.statement: secp256k1 has a kernel-checked order-three GLV endomorphism whose affine x-coordinate action is multiplication by a nontrivial cube root of unity.
target_features.boundary: The order-three orbit gives a known constant-factor structure; by itself it neither preserves a fixed target nor changes an asymptotic exponent.

target_features.label: the explicit prime-field coordinate representation
target_features.statement: The plain target exposes prime-field curve coordinates and arithmetic outside the generic-group oracle model, so a legitimate classical escape must identify exactly which representation information it consumes.
target_features.boundary: Access to coordinates is only an opportunity surface. It is not evidence that relation generation, generalized root finding, or descent is cheaper than the square-root baseline.

target_features.label: the low-degree composed-map factor-base construction
target_features.statement: Petit-style factor bases define x-coordinates through a low-degree composition, creating structured fibers whose relation yield and generalized root-solving cost can be measured independently.
target_features.boundary: A smaller coordinate image or a successful toy solve is not a complexity improvement unless recovery, exceptional fibers, preprocessing, and total relation cost are all included.

mechanism_primitives.label: a phase-preserving faithful quotient with recovery
mechanism_primitives.statement: Use invariants or a birational presentation that preserves relative GLV phases, fixed-target relation semantics, exceptional components, and an explicit recovery map.
mechanism_primitives.boundary: Independent coordinate cubes are excluded. More variables or a toric invariant ring do not count as a gain without an audited reduction in total solving cost.

mechanism_primitives.label: summation-polynomial relation sampling with complete costs
mechanism_primitives.statement: Generate factor-base relations through exact Semaev systems while measuring relation probability, algebraic solving effort, recovery failures, linear algebra, and rejected components.
mechanism_primitives.boundary: Polynomial degree, matrix size, or one solver timing is only a proxy and cannot establish a subgeneric algorithm without an end-to-end cost bridge.

mechanism_primitives.label: generalized root finding with explicit fiber recovery
mechanism_primitives.statement: Exploit a composed rational map only through an algorithm that enumerates or samples valid fibers, recovers curve points, prices excluded components, and returns independently checkable relations.
mechanism_primitives.boundary: The construction remains a proposal primitive until its generalized root problem and all offline work are cheaper than the matched plain presentation at increasing toy sizes.

unresolved_questions.label: whether a faithful GLV presentation changes solving cost rather than notation
unresolved_questions.statement: No exact phase-preserving fixed-target presentation currently demonstrates a lower solving degree, relation cost, or total index-calculus exponent than the plain system.
unresolved_questions.boundary: The closed independent-cube quotient may not be reopened without a new premise, and finite target batching alone is not an asymptotic bridge.

unresolved_questions.label: whether prime-field relation generation changes the square-root exponent
unresolved_questions.statement: The repository lacks a source-grounded mechanism and cost theorem connecting prime-field summation-polynomial relation yield to total work below the Pollard-rho square-root baseline.
unresolved_questions.boundary: Toy relations, proxy matrices, and informal asymptotics remain insufficient until the factor-base probability, solver, recovery, linear algebra, and precomputation terms are joined.

unresolved_questions.label: whether the composed-map generalized root problem scales better end to end
unresolved_questions.statement: The faithful Petit-style route has no validated algorithm showing that generalized root finding plus recovery and preprocessing beats the matched plain factor-base pipeline as field size grows.
unresolved_questions.boundary: Approximate or nonfaithful variants and isolated toy wins do not answer the faithful generalized-root question.
